Walk-off is the largest beam-separation angle of the three waves (spatial walk-off). The pulse separation (GVM) is the largest group-velocity mismatch of the three waves: the pulses separate by this many femtoseconds per mm of crystal, so for a pulse τ the useful crystal length is about τ/GVM (the next column, for a 100 fs pulse). The acceptance widths (FWHM) are for a 1 cm crystal; for an L cm crystal divide by about L (by √L for noncritical phase matching).

From it come the heralded-photon purity (P = Σλₙ²), the Schmidt number K = 1/P, the spectral width of each photon and the Hong–Ou–Mandel dip. The refractive indices are the formulas of the phase-matching tab. Tested against Fig. 1 of Mosley et al. (2008) and the Schmidt number of Evans et al. (2010). Gaussian apodized poling (Brańczyk et al. 2011) removes the sinc side lobes; “Optimize purity” finds the pump bandwidth of the highest purity; with a crystal temperature the indices come from the source's temperature-dependent formula (if it has one).

آنچه دو آشکارساز تک‌فوتون از این چشمه‌ی: What two single-photon detectors count from this CW source: the pair rate R (card above, same ξ) and the conditional fibre couplings μ (fibre card), times each arm's transmission (optics, filter, fibre) and detector efficiency, plus dark counts. Accidental coincidences A = S₁·S₂·τ (two unrelated counts in one window), and CAR = C/A. The heralding (Klyshko) efficiency is the chance that a photon is detected when its twin was. Since C grows linearly with pump power and A quadratically, the CAR has a maximum set by the dark counts; the powers that reach a target CAR are given too.
